mainTopic: Does a כהן own a living unblemished בכור, and may he sell one to a ישראל?
overview: This amud asks whether a כהן owns an unblemished בכור while it is still alive. אביי and רבינא explain that sources saying he owns it are talking about a בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון, because there is no duty to bring that one to the מזבח. The גמרא suggests this may be an argument between תנאים in a ברייתא. It answers that the ברייתא is just the same dispute as רבי יוחנן בן נורי and רבי עקיבא in the משנה. Next, רב חסדא rules that a living unblemished בכור may be sold only from one כהן to another, not to a ישראל. His reason is challenged, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a new reason: it looks like a כהן helping at the threshing floor to earn gifts. In a story, מר זוטרא questions his hosts at רב אשי's house for buying a בכור from a כהן. They answer that a real, paid purchase is different, and the explanation of the כהן's thinking continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי: the case is an unblemished firstborn from outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the earlier difficulty. The ברייתא is about an unblemished בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: No. The ברייתא really is about an unblemished animal. It is a firstborn from outside ארץ ישראל, and it follows רבי שמעון, who said: if unblemished ones were brought, they are offered.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new way to read the ברייתא, so it no longer clashes with the idea that a כהן does not own an unblemished בכור. He says it is talking about a special kind of בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal unblemished בכור from ארץ ישראל must go on the מזבח, so the כהן does not fully own it. But רבי שמעון holds that a בכור from חוץ לארץ is offered only if someone happens to bring it. There is no duty to bring it, so the כהן can own it even while it is unblemished.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (it is still the same case as before)
An unblemished animal
A firstborn animal, which is given to a כהן
Outside ארץ ישראל
They are offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's words 'if they came, they are offered' do not mean you must bring them. They mean only that if someone did bring them, they go on the מזבח. That is exactly why the כהן can own them.

phrases.english: Abaye said: No,
actually it is about an unblemished animal,
and about a firstborn outside Eretz Yisrael,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon, who said:
If unblemished ones came, they are offered.
phrases.notes: He means firstborns that someone brought from outside Eretz Yisrael. Bringing them is not required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised before this section by placing the ברייתא in a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא had to be about a blemished בכור, or else it would show that a כהן owns any unblemished בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about an unblemished בכור from חוץ לארץ. That one the כהן owns, because there is no duty to offer it.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן בן נורי in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who says a כהן owns a בכור in its lifetime. It proves that he must mean an unblemished one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said to him: What does it prove to me? If a priest does not make substitutes with a sin offering and a guilt offering, which priests do not own while they are alive, can you say the same about a firstborn, which they do own while it is alive? What case are we dealing with? If you say a blemished one, he is comparing it to a sin offering and a guilt offering! So is it not about an unblemished one? And it teaches that the priests own it while it is alive!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that a כהן does not own an unblemished בכור. It uses רבי יוחנן בן נורי's words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the כהן owns the בכור while it is alive. The גמרא asks which בכור he means. It cannot be a blemished one, because he is setting it side by side with חטאת and אשם, which are unblemished offerings. So he must mean an unblemished בכור, and he still says the כהן owns it.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a תמורה, swapping an animal for a holy one
Sin offering and guilt offering
The כהנים own it while it is still alive
What case are we dealing with?
A blemished animal
Similar to, set side by side with

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: They challenged: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי עקיבא. In the משנה he compared a firstborn to a sin offering and a guilt offering.

phrases.english: What does it prove to me? If he does not make a substitute
with a sin offering and a guilt offering,
since priests do not own them while they are alive,
will you say the same about a firstborn, which they own while it is alive?
What case are we dealing with?
If you say with a blemished animal,
but he is speaking of it as similar to a sin offering and a guilt offering!
Rather, is it not about an unblemished one,
and it teaches that they own it while it is alive!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that seems to show a כהן owns even a normal unblemished בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a כהן does not own an unblemished בכור during its life, except in a special case like אביי's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן בן נורי compares the בכור to unblemished חטאת and אשם, so he must mean an unblemished בכור. Yet he says the כהן owns it in its lifetime.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה is also about a firstborn from outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers the same way אביי did. רבי יוחנן בן נורי is also talking about a בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This too is about a firstborn outside ארץ ישראל, and it follows רבי שמעון, who said: if unblemished ones came, they are offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends the view against the challenge. He reads רבי יוחנן בן נורי's case as the same special case אביי used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge showed that רבי יוחנן בן נורי means an unblemished בכור. רבינא agrees with that, but limits it to a בכור from חוץ לארץ, which there is no duty to offer. So the rule still stands: a כהן does not own an unblemished בכור from ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too (is the same special case)
Unblemished animals

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבינא handle sources that say 'the כהן owns the בכור' the same way. Those sources are about an unblemished בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון. A כהן does not own an unblemished בכור from ארץ ישראל while it is alive.

phrases.english: Ravina said: This too
phrases.notes: 'This' is רבי יוחנן בן נורי's statement in the משנה from the previous step.

phrases.english: is about a firstborn outside Eretz Yisrael,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon, who said:
If unblemished ones came, they are offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: הָא נָמֵי בִּבְכוֹר בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה using the same approach as אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a בכור from חוץ לארץ, following רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן בן נורי seemed to say a כהן owns any unblemished בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is talking only about an unblemished בכור from חוץ לארץ, which the כהן can own.

steps.title: Is this question an argument between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that whether a כהן owns a בכור may be an argument between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about a בכור in the owner's house versus the כהן's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is like an argument between תנאים: A firstborn, while it is in the owner's house, one can make a substitute with it. Once it is in the priest's house, one cannot make a substitute with it. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: once it has come into the priest's hands, one cannot make a substitute with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new suggestion: maybe תנאים already argued about this question. It quotes the ברייתא here and will explain the argument in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the owner can make a תמורה while the בכור is still in his own house, but not once it is in the כהן's house. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the owner loses this power as soon as the animal comes into the כהן's hands. The גמרא is about to explain how these two views connect to whether the כהן owns the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is an argument between תנאים?
A substitute animal that becomes holy in place of a holy one
The owner's house, before the animal is given to the כהן
As soon as it has come into the כהן's hands

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions sound almost the same. The difference is in the wording: 'in the כהן's house' versus 'came into the כהן's hands.' The גמרא will explain what that difference means next, so do not try to settle it yet.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like an argument between Tannaim:
A firstborn, while in the owner's house,
one can make a substitute with it,
in the priest's house, one cannot make a substitute with it.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Once it has come into the priest's hands,
one cannot make a substitute with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the view, the גמרא looks for whether the same question was argued among תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the question of whether a כהן owns a בכור in its lifetime an argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?

steps.title: Reading the first opinion to show the כהן owns the בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר seems to say the same thing as the תנא קמא. So it reads the תנא קמא as saying that in the כהן's house, the כהן can do תמורה and the owner cannot. That shows the תנא קמא holds the כהן owns the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is just what the first opinion said! Isn't the first opinion really saying this: once the animal is in the כהן's house, the כהן can make a substitute and the original owner cannot? So the first opinion holds that the כהן owns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from the ברייתא in the last step. It shows that the first opinion in that ברייתא holds a כהן owns a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions said the same thing, there would be nothing to argue about. So the תנא קמא must mean that in the כהן's house, the כהן can do תמורה. Only an owner can do תמורה, so the כהן must own the animal. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees, which means the question really is a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Isn't it that…? This opens a suggested reading.
Apparently / this shows that
Ownership rights

phrases.english: That is the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view in the ברייתא sounds just like the first opinion. So what are they arguing about?

phrases.english: Is it not that this is what he is saying:
In the priest's house, he can make a substitute,
but the owner cannot make a substitute.
Apparently, the priest has
ownership rights in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא! מַאי לָאו הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the suggestion from step 4 by reading the ברייתא so that it shows a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the ownership of a כהן over a בכור is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a בכור in the owner's house versus the כהן's house, read so the two opinions do not say the same thing

steps.title: No problem: the ברייתא is just the משנה's dispute between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this is no problem. The first opinion follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not a difficulty. This first opinion follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and that other opinion follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא causes no difficulty. Its two opinions are the same dispute as רבי יוחנן בן נורי and רבי עקיבא in the משנה, which was already explained as being about a בכור from חוץ לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion, that the כהן owns the בכור, follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who disagrees, follows רבי עקיבא. רבינא already explained in step 3 that רבי יוחנן בן נורי is talking about a בכור from חוץ לארץ, so this ברייתא proves nothing about a בכור from ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty
This one… that one… This sorts two sources between two different opinions.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's dispute is the same as the משנה's dispute between רבי יוחנן בן נורי (the כהן owns it) and רבי עקיבא (he does not). That dispute is only about a בכור from חוץ לארץ. An unblemished בכור from ארץ ישראל is not owned by the כהן according to everyone.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one follows Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri,
phrases.notes: This is the first opinion of the ברייתא, the one that says the כהן owns it.

phrases.english: and that one follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the reading from step 5 and names which earlier תנאים each side follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the ברייתא to an already-explained dispute (רבי יוחנן בן נורי vs. רבי עקיבא, set in חוץ לארץ)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא of the ברייתא seemed to hold that a כהן owns any unblemished בכור, which would challenge the view defended in steps 1–3.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא repeats the רבי יוחנן בן נורי / רבי עקיבא dispute, which is about a בכור from חוץ לארץ. So a כהן still does not own an unblemished בכור from ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a כהן may sell a live unblemished בכור only to another כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the rule that an unblemished בכור may be sold while it is alive. It applies only from a כהן to another כהן. Selling to a ישראל is forbidden, because he might make a מום himself and claim it came that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: That rule was taught only about a כהן selling to another כהן. But a כהן selling to a ישראל is forbidden. Why? The ישראל might go and make a blemish in the animal. Then he would bring it to a חכם and say, "A כהן gave me this בכור with its blemish already."
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. רב חסדא narrows an earlier ruling that a live, unblemished בכור may be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל may eat a בכור only if it has a מום. So if he owns one, he might be tempted to make a מום himself, which is forbidden. Then he would tell the חכם it already had the מום when he got it. A כהן buying from a כהן has no such reason to cheat, so that sale is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about… This limits an earlier rule.
What is the reason?
Perhaps / there is a worry that
A physical blemish. It disqualifies an animal from the מזבח and lets a בכור be eaten.
A rabbi who examines a בכור to see if its blemish counts

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
They taught this only about a priest selling to a priest,
phrases.notes: "This" is the earlier משנה that lets an unblemished בכור be sold while it is still alive.

phrases.english: but a priest selling to an Israelite is forbidden.
What is the reason?
Perhaps the Israelite will go
and inflict a blemish on it,
and bring it to a Sage, and say to him:
"A priest gave me this firstborn with its blemish."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כֹּהֵן לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic. It narrows an earlier-quoted ruling about selling a living unblemished בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A live unblemished בכור may be sold only from a כהן to a כהן, not to a ישראל, because he might make a מום and lie about it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit on who may buy a living unblemished בכור. The rest of the section tests whether the worry behind it is real.

steps.title: Would a חכם even allow this? רב requires a כהן to be present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's worry. רב said a חכם does not examine a ישראל's בכור unless a כהן is there with him, so the lie would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But would a חכם allow it in a case like this? Didn't רב say that a חכם does not examine a בכור for a ישראל unless a כהן is with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason רב חסדא gave in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא worried that the ישראל could fool the חכם. But according to רב, the חכם would not even look at the animal without a כהן present. The כהן who sold it could then tell the truth about whether it had a מום, so the worry seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And would he really allow it? This opens a challenge.
They do not examine. Here it means a חכם checking a בכור's blemish.
Unless

phrases.english: And would a Sage permit it like this?
But didn't Rav say:
We do not examine a firstborn for an Israelite
unless a priest is with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שָׁרֵי חָכָם הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רב חסדא gave in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's worry that a ישראל could fool a חכם about a blemish he made himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב says a חכם only examines a ישראל's בכור when a כהן is present. So the ישראל could not get away with his lie, and the reason for the ban seems to fall away.

steps.title: A new reason: it looks like a כהן helping at the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the real reason a ישראל may not buy an unblemished בכור is that it looks like a כהן helping at the threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: This is the reason a ישראל is forbidden to buy it: because it looks like a כהן who helps out at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא's reason (the ישראל might fake a מום) was knocked down in step 8. Now רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a new reason for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule stays the same: a כהן may not sell an unblemished בכור to a ישראל. Only the reason changes. Instead of worrying about cheating with a מום, the worry is how it looks: the כהן seems to be doing the ישראל a favor so he will get gifts later, like a כהן who helps at the threshing floor to get תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
A כהן who helps at the threshing floors, hoping to be given the gifts in return
Threshing floors, where grain is processed and תרומה is separated

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason is the key that the whole story after it turns on.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
This is the reason that it is forbidden to a Yisrael,
phrases.notes: He means it is forbidden for a כהן to sell an unblemished בכור to a ישראל, the rule from step 7.

phrases.english: because it looks like a kohen
who helps out at the threshing floors.
phrases.notes: A כהן who pitches in at a farmer's threshing floor looks like he is earning his תרומה, and that is not proper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reason for רב חסדא's rule after his reason was challenged in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason for the same rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban rested on the worry that the ישראל would make a מום himself, and רב's rule takes that worry away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban rests on how it looks: the כהן seems to be helping in order to get gifts.

steps.title: מר זוטרא is served בכור meat at רב אשי's house
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא visits רב אשי and is served בכור meat. He asks where it came from and is told a כהן sold it to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא came to רב אשי's house. They said to him: Let the master taste something. They brought meat before him. Someone said: Let the master eat, because it is healthy, since it is a בכור. He asked: Where did you get this? They said: A certain כהן sold it to us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next move. מר זוטרא learns that his hosts bought a בכור from a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case of רב הונא's rule: a ישראל buying a בכור from a כהן. Asking where the meat came from prepares the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come, visited
Healthy, good for the body
A בכור, a firstborn animal
So-and-so, a certain person

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: Mar Zutra came to the house of Rav Ashi.
They said to him: Let the master taste something.
They brought meat before him.
He said to him: Let the master eat,
for it is healthy, because it is a firstborn.
From where do you have this?
phrases.notes: מר זוטרא is the one asking here.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: דְּזַבֵּן לַן פְּלוֹנִי כֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: They said to him: So-and-so the kohen sold it to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life story that tests רב הונא's rule from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story sets up a real case: a ישראל who bought a בכור from a כהן.

steps.title: מר זוטרא asks: don't you follow רב הונא's rule?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges his hosts. Buying a בכור from a כהן should be forbidden because of רב הונא's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Don't you hold like what רב הונא son of רב יהושע said, that it is forbidden because it looks like a כהן helping at the threshing floors?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא uses רב הונא's rule from step 9 to question why the household bought this בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is simple: this is exactly the case רב הונא forbade. A ישראל bought a בכור from a כהן, so it should look like the כהן is helping in order to get gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't you hold (that opinion)?
That it looks like, how it appears to others

phrases.english: He said to them: Don't you hold

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: that which Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן הַמְסַיֵּיעַ בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת?
phrases.english: because it looks like a kohen who helps out at the threshing floors?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סְבִירָא לְכוּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב הונא's rule to the story and challenges what the hosts did.
steps.kashyaTarget: The hosts' purchase of a בכור from a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא forbids a ישראל to get a בכור from a כהן because it looks like the כהן is helping to get gifts.

steps.title: The hosts answer: we paid full price
steps.stepSummary: The hosts say רב הונא's concern does not apply to them because they bought the בכור at its full value.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We don't hold that it applies here, because we bought it with a real sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts defend themselves. They paid full price, so the כהן did them no favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read רב הונא's worry as being about a discount: a cheap price looks like a favor to win future gifts. If the ישראל pays the full price, nothing looks like a favor, so they think the concern goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: We truly bought it, as a real sale at full value

phrases.english: They said to him: We don't hold so,
phrases.notes: They mean the concern doesn't fit their case, not that they reject רב הונא.

phrases.english: for we really bought it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge by narrowing רב הונא's concern.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the concern applies only to a discount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any purchase of a בכור by a ישראל from a כהן looks like a favor.
steps.terutzMaskana: A purchase at full value is not a favor, so it should be allowed.

steps.title: מר זוטרא pushes back with a משנה about caring for a בכור
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא quotes a משנה: a ישראל must care for a בכור for a set time and may not give it to the כהן early. רב ששת explains this is because of the threshing-floor concern, even though no money changes hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Don't you hold what we learned in a משנה: How long must a ישראל take care of a בכור? A small animal, thirty days; a large animal, fifty days. And if the כהן said to him: Give it to me within its time, he may not give it to him. And רב ששת said: What is the reason? Because it looks like a כהן helping at the threshing floors!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges the hosts' answer. He brings a case where the threshing-floor concern applies even without any discount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the כהן takes the בכור early and saves the ישראל the work of caring for it. רב ששת says even this small favor is forbidden because it looks like helping at the threshing floor. So the concern is any favor at all, not only a discount, and paying full price may not be enough to make the sale fine.

keyTerms.meaning: To take care of, look after
A small animal (sheep or goat)
A large animal (cattle)
Within its time, before the care period is over

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא argues that the threshing-floor concern applies even without a discount. The hosts answer this in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: In the משנה, the one asking to take the בכור early is the כהן, not the ישראל. The favor is that the כהן takes the care burden off the ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְלָא סְבִירָא לְכוּ הָדִתְנַן:
phrases.english: He said to them: And don't you hold that which we learned:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיב לִיטַּפֵּל בַּבְּכוֹר?
phrases.english: Until how long is a Yisrael obligated to take care of a firstborn?
For a small animal, thirty days,
and for a large animal, fifty days.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי בְּתוֹךְ זְמַנּוֹ״ —
phrases.english: And if he said to him: Give it to me within its time,
phrases.notes: The כהן is speaking to the owner.

phrases.english: he should not give it to him.
And Rav Sheshet said: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן הַמְסַיֵּיעַ בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת!
phrases.english: Because it looks like a kohen who helps out at the threshing floors!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hosts' claim that paying full price removes the concern.
steps.kashyaTarget: The hosts' answer that a full-price sale is fine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה no discount is involved, only the כהן saving the ישראל work, and רב ששת still forbids it because of the threshing-floor concern. So any favor counts, and a full-price sale may still be a problem.

steps.title: The hosts answer: in the משנה's case the favor is obvious, but we bought it
steps.stepSummary: The hosts tell מר זוטרא that in the משנה's case it is plain to see that the כהן is doing a favor to get the animal. They bought the בכור in a normal sale, so it does not look like a favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There, the matter is obvious. Here, we actually bought it.
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts answer מר זוטרא's challenge from step 13. They say the משנה's case is different from theirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, when the כהן takes the young בכור and raises it himself, everyone can see he is doing work to get the animal. That looks like a כהן helping at the threshing floor. A normal purchase at a fair price shows no such favor, so there is nothing to suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: There (here, the case in the משנה)
The matter is obvious; it is plain to see
We actually bought it (a real sale)

phrases.english: They said to him:
There, the matter is obvious;
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה's case, where the כהן takes the young בכור early and raises it.

phrases.english: here, we actually bought it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the משנה brought in step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ban, which applies even with no payment, should also ban buying a בכור from a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's case clearly looks like a favor. A real purchase does not.

steps.title: A second version of the answer: here money is paid
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the hosts say the difference is about money. In the משנה's case the person gives nothing for the כהן's work, but here the buyers pay the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: They said to him: There, he does not give money. Here, he does give money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of how the hosts answered מר זוטרא. This one points to payment as the key difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the כהן is not paid for raising the animal. His only reward is getting the בכור, so it looks like he is earning it. In a sale, the buyer pays real money, so the deal is a fair exchange and not a favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version (of the same discussion)
Gives money; pays

phrases.english: Another version: they said to him:
Here, he does not give money;
phrases.notes: This first "here" is really about the משנה's case. Nobody pays the כהן for raising the animal there.

phrases.english: here, he does give money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the answer in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) based on payment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Buying from a כהן is just like the משנה's case, so it should be banned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying money makes it a fair deal. The משנה's case had no payment.

steps.title: A worry: maybe the כהן gives a discount hoping for the next בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what someone might say against the payment answer. Maybe the כהן sells the בכור cheaply because he hopes the buyer will give him their next בכור. Then it would still look like buying a favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say? That the כהן lowers the price for him, because the כהן thinks that when the buyer has another בכור, he will give it to him?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the second version, the hosts raise a possible objection to their own answer: paying money might not be enough if the כהן lowered the price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן gives a discount to get future gifts, part of the payment is not real money. That missing part would be a favor, which brings back the threshing-floor concern. The question tests whether "they paid" truly removes the concern.

keyTerms.meaning: What would you say? (raising a possible objection)
Lowers the price; gives a discount
Another firstborn animal

phrases.english: What would you say?
that the כהן lowers the price for him,
because the כהן thinks
that when he has another בכור
he will give it to him?
phrases.notes: "He" is the buyer, who would give his future בכור to this כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The hosts anticipate an objection to their own payment answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that paying money removes the threshing-floor concern
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lowered price hides a favor inside the sale, so the concern would come back.

steps.title: No, because the כהן is thinking something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the discount worry and begins to explain what the כהן really thinks. The explanation continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the discount worry by saying "no." This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will say what the כהן is really thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "no" rejects the idea that the כהן gives a discount hoping for future gifts. The reason, which is what the כהן has in mind, is spelled out in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: He thinks; it comes to his mind

phrases.english: No, because he thinks:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the discount worry from step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the assumption about what the כהן intends
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן lowers the price hoping for future בכורות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן does not think this way. His real thought is explained next.
